# Draft:G. Edward DeSeve

----
G. Edward DeSeve (born 1945) is an American public official and academic who has served at multiple levels of government. He was the Chief Financial Officer of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development from 1993 to 1994  and later held senior roles in the White House Office of Management and Budget, including Controller (1994–1997) and Deputy Director for Management (1997–1999). In 2009, President Barack Obama appointed DeSeve as a Special Advisor overseeing the implementation of the $787 billion American Recovery and Reinvestment Act, a role in which he coordinated the federal stimulus program. DeSeve's career also includes service in state and local government, notably as Director of Finance for the City of Philadelphia, and work in the private sector and academia. He is currently an Executive Fellow at the IBM Center for the Business of Government and the Coordinator of the Agile Government Center at the National Academy of Public Administration.
Early Life and Education
DeSeve was born in 1945. He earned a Bachelor of Science in labor economics from Cornell University's School of Industrial and Labor Relations in 1967, and a Master of Government Administration in public finance from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania in 1971. After completing his education, DeSeve joined Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA) in 1968, working with credit unions in rural California, and then began a career in public finance and administration.
Career
Local and state government
DeSeve started his career in city government in the early 1970s in Philadelphia. He worked on the city's Community Renewal Program and financial management systems, and by 1974 he became Deputy Director of Finance for Budget for the City of Philadelphia. In 1980, Mayor William J. Green III appointed DeSeve as the Director of Finance for Philadelphia, a position he held from 1980 to 1982. During his tenure, he helped the city navigate a period of fiscal crisis and implement measures to stabilize the city's finances. From 1990 to 1992, DeSeve served as a Special Assistant to the Governor of Pennsylvania, Robert P. Casey, focusing on state budget and finance issues. In that role he chaired several state financing authorities and contributed to oversight of state agencies.
Federal government service
In 1993, President Bill Clinton nominated DeSeve as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). After Senate confirmation in July 1993, DeSeve served as HUD's CFO until 1994, establishing financial management policies and producing the department's first audited financial statements. He then moved to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) in the Executive Office of the President. DeSeve was OMB Controller from 1994 to 1997, where he coordinated financial management improvements across federal agencies. In May 1997, he was appointed OMB's Deputy Director for Management, the senior official in charge of federal management and administration, serving until 1999. During his OMB tenure, DeSeve played a key role in federal financial reforms – he chaired the President's Management Council and the Chief Financial Officers Council, and he helped coordinate the government's preparation for the Year 2000 (Y2K) computer challenge. He also oversaw fiscal turnaround efforts for the District of Columbia, which led to improved credit ratings and budget surpluses for the D.C. government.
After leaving OMB in 1999, DeSeve briefly worked in the private sector (see below) before returning to federal service in 2009. In March 2009, he was appointed by the Obama administration as Special Advisor to the President and Assistant to the Vice President for implementation of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA). In this capacity – informally dubbed the "stimulus czar" – DeSeve coordinated the interagency effort to disburse the $787 billion stimulus package, working under Vice President Joe Biden's leadership to ensure funds were allocated quickly and with oversight. He directed the Recovery Act implementation team until 2011, overseeing reporting on the Act's progress and compliance by funding recipients. The ARRA program was widely credited with successful administration of funds, and DeSeve's work alongside Biden was later cited as a model of effective federal coordination.
Private sector
Outside of government, DeSeve has had a significant career in finance and consulting. In 1975, he founded Public Financial Management, Inc. (PFM), which grew to become the nation's largest independent financial advisory firm serving state and local governments. He was president of PFM from 1975 to 1980, advising numerous states and municipalities on bond issuances and fiscal management. After working in Philadelphia's government, DeSeve joined Merrill Lynch Capital Markets as a managing director from 1982 to 1985, overseeing municipal finance activities in a multi-state region. In the late 1990s, following his OMB service, he became a partner and National Industry Director for the federal practice at KPMG Peat Marwick (1999–2000).
DeSeve also co-founded Governmentum Partners, a consulting firm focused on helping governments implement technology and management improvements, which was later acquired by Affiliated Computer Services (ACS). He served as a Senior Vice President at ACS's government services division in the 2000s. In recent years, DeSeve has been a Senior Advisor with GovNavigators, a consulting group, while continuing to engage in public sector advisory roles.
Academic career
DeSeve has held academic appointments at several institutions. From 2000 to 2006, he was a tenured Professor of the Practice of Public Management and Finance at the University of Maryland, College Park, where he directed the Management, Finance and Leadership program at the School of Public Policy. He also taught public management and financial administration as a Senior Lecturer at the University of Pennsylvania's Fels Institute of Government, in two periods during 1985–1993 and 2006–2009. In 2011, after his work on the Recovery Act, DeSeve joined the Brookings Institution's Executive Education program as an Executive in Residence, contributing to leadership training for government executives. He has also been a guest instructor or fellow at other universities – for example, he held adjunct teaching assignments at Carnegie Mellon University and the Australian National University in the early 2010s. Throughout his academic career, DeSeve has focused on public finance, public management, and leadership, mentoring future public administrators by drawing on his extensive government experience.
Publications
DeSeve is the author or co-author of numerous works on public administration, financial management, and governance. His notable publications include:
* ''The Presidential Appointee's Handbook (Brookings Institution Press, 1st ed. 2008, 2nd ed. 2017) – a guide for senior federal appointees on management competencies.
* Managing Recovery: An Insider's View (IBM Center for the Business of Government, 2011) – an account of the implementation of the Recovery Act.
* Enhancing Government Decision Making (IBM Center for the Business of Government, 2016) – a study on improving management information for decision-makers.
* An Agile Tipping Point (IBM Center for the Business of Government, 2019) – a report on adopting agile practices in government.
* The Road to Agile Government (IBM Center for the Business of Government, 2020) – a follow-up report on transforming public leadership for agility.
Earlier in his career, DeSeve also co-authored A Financial Management Handbook for Mayors and City Managers (Van Nostrand Reinhold, 1985) and contributed articles to journals such as Government Finance Review and The Public Manager'', reflecting his long-standing involvement in public financial management reforms.
Awards and honors
DeSeve has received several awards and honors in recognition of his public service and professional contributions:
* George Graham Award for Exceptional Service – awarded by the National Academy of Public Administration (NAPA) in 2021, honoring his lifetime service to the Academy. DeSeve is a NAPA Fellow (since 1995) and served as the Academy's Vice Chair, contributing to its studies on fiscal future and agile government initiatives.
* S. Kenneth Howard Award – given by the American Society for Public Administration (ASPA) in 2002, recognizing DeSeve's career achievements in public financial management.
* Federal 100 Award – named one of the Federal Computer Week "Fed 100" in 2021 for his work in improving federal IT and agile government, particularly as Coordinator of NAPA's Agile Government Center.
* Federal Information Technology Hall of Fame – inducted in 2000 by Government Computer News for his contributions to federal IT and management leadership during his OMB tenure (notably his Y2K coordination efforts).
* HUD Outstanding Achievement Award (1994) – awarded by the Department of Housing and Urban Development for his service as CFO, along with earlier honors such as the Association of Government Accountants Achievement Award (1998) and the '''OMB Director's Award for Outstanding Service''' (1999) for his federal service.
Affiliations
DeSeve is an active member of professional organizations and initiatives in public administration. In addition to his fellowship at NAPA, he is an Executive Fellow at the IBM Center for the Business of Government, where he contributes research on government effectiveness. He also co-chairs the Agile Government Center (a joint venture of NAPA and the IBM Center) to promote agile practices in public governance. Earlier, he founded and serves as president of the Global Public Leadership Institute, a network aimed at supporting public sector leaders worldwide. DeSeve's multi-level government experience and continued involvement in think tanks and academic programs have made him a recognized expert on improving government performance and financial stewardship.
